:::{#exm-complex-arithmetic}
#### Adding and multiplying two complex numbers

Let $w = 1 + 2\,i$ and $z = 3 - i$.
Their sum is

$$
\ba
w + z
&= (1 + 3) + (2 + (-1))\,i
&& \text{(@thm-complex-arithmetic, sum)}
\\
&= 4 + i
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

and their product, multiplying out directly, is

$$
\ba
w z
&= 1 \cd 3 + 1 \cd (-i) + 2\,i \cd 3 + 2\,i \cd (-i)
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= 3 - i + 6\,i - 2\,i^2
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= 3 - i + 6\,i + 2
&& \text{(@def-imaginary-unit)}
\\
&= (3 + 2) + (-1 + 6)\,i
&& \text{(group the real terms and the terms with } i \text{)}
\\
&= 5 + 5\,i
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

The product formula in @thm-complex-arithmetic gives the same answer:
with $a = 1$, $b = 2$, $c = 3$ and $d = -1$,
$ac - bd = 3 - (-2) = 5$
and $ad + bc = -1 + 6 = 5$.

:::
